title: 47th Civil Engineering Squadron Fire Flight
description: U.S. Air Force Airman William Joy, 47th Civil Engineering Squadron Fire Flight firefighter, speaks about the responsibilities of his flight at Laughlin Air Force Base, Texas, Jan. 13, 2023. Joy demonstrated how the Fire Flight provides Laughlin AFB with the skills and knowledge to stay safe during a fire; whether at home, work or in a deployed location. (U.S. Air Force video by Airman 1st Class Kailee Reynolds)

transcript.text: Fire protection supports the civil
engineering squadron in completing
their mission by providing efficient
fire and emergency services to the
people of Laughlin Air Force Base . Not
only the crash side with the runway ,
but also the structural side as well .
My day to day here as a firefighter ,
my day starts at seven AM for a shift
change . And from 7 to 8 AM , we pull
all the trucks out and inspect all of
our equipment and make sure everything
is working properly . After that , we
usually go out and train in the
mornings and do exercises at the fire
tower or the burn pit over with the
plane . And in the afternoon , we
usually allot time to maintain the fire
station . If that's washing trucks or
hose testing , does anything to help
maintain the fire station , keep
everything running smoothly . The thing
I enjoy most about my job as a
firefighter would definitely have to be
the camaraderie between me and my other
firefighters on shift , living together
48 hours at a time . Really just brings
everyone together . It feels great to
be able to help our pilots , service
members and their families and it's an
honor to be a part of something much
bigger than myself .
